title: Transit Only
hook: One-way. No turn on red. Transit only.
scene: Wet overcast on a downtown block. Three faces sit over the same intersection: a black-and-white ONE WAY arrow, a NO TURN ON RED, and a TRANSIT ONLY over the left lane. The left is empty and faster. Your clock likes empty. The paint and the faces already spent that argument. The Menace is one car. Transit only is not a suggestion for a Beetle with a plow.
decision: The left is empty and posted transit only. Which restriction do you obey?

options.text: Stay out of the transit lane, no turn on red, go the way the one-way points
options.result: You hold the general lane. Red stays red for your right. The empty transit lane stays empty. A bus remnant takes it two breaths later. The faces were the sentence.

options.text: Take the empty transit lane — nothing is coming and you are through traffic
options.result: You take the diamond's cousin. A bus remnant is already committed. You write a Beetle into a lane that was never yours. The remnant has to lift. Downtown remembers the plow in the wrong paint.

options.text: Turn right on the red — the one-way is clear and waiting costs you the block
options.result: You take the red. The sign said no. A figure you did not have is already in that crosswalk. You invent a stop you were told not to skip.

options.text: Go the wrong way on the one-way for one block to skip the transit restriction
options.result: You point the plow at oncoming. Wet pavement and a pair of lamps. One-way is not a puzzle you get to rewrite because the left was posted.

debrief: Downtown signs stack. One-way, no turn on red, transit only — each one is in force even if the lane looks empty. Stay out of the transit lane.

source.psdp_skill: Skill ten: city driving – part one
source.teaching_target: Obey stacked downtown signs: one-way direction, no turn on red, and transit-only lane restrictions.
